I agree with the core premises we all seem to be using now – the first move is forced to be 1.N1 1-3 and the only checking weapon is the rook, so the whole game is about keeping the two kings off the enemy rook line. K1 is screened by N1-R1 and K2 is screened by R2-N2 and a move is legal only if the mover’s own king stays rook-free after the move.

On 1.N1 1-3 the three king-safe replies are 1…R2 5-4, 1…N2 6-4 and the blunder 1…R2 5×3. The 5-ply 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 3.R1×N2# line is real, it is the cooperative textbook mate, and it is why the 5-ply/7-ply illustrations get quoted.

It is not forceable against perfect stalling. Black never gives up the 1…R2×N1 capture. With the best defence the centre can be kept closed by the N2 6↔4 shuttle and the R2 5↔4 shuttle.

One maximal-stall net is

1.N1 1-3      1…R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2…N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3…R2 4-3
4.R1 4-3×R2   4…N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5…N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#

K1 is never left in the R2 line: after 1.N1 1-3 R1 2 still blocks 0–R2, after 2.R1 2-4 N1 3 blocks 0–R2, after 3.N1 3-5 R1 4 blocks 0–R2 and after 4.R1 4-3×R2 N1 5 now blocks the line to the now removed R2. K2 is never left in the R1 line: N2 6-4 keeps a blocker on the R1-K2 file, N2 4-6 restores it after the rook advance, and N2 6-4 is forced again before the final capture.

The N2 6-4-6-4 shuttle is the unavoidable waiting resource. The 7-ply lines that are being quoted skip the second N2 return. Once the rook is on 4 it cannot go to 6 while N2 is on 4, because 4…K2 7-6 would walk K2 into the R1 4–6 line – illegal under the king-safety rule – and 4…N2 4-2 would expose K2 to R1 4 on the next White move. The knight therefore has to go back to 6, costing White a tempo, and the same happens again on the next rook advance.

That is exactly the two extra tempi that separate the cooperative 5-ply mate from the forced mate under optimal stalling. Counting a half-move as a turn the first check that cannot be met is delivered on White’s 5th move, the 9th half-move of the game. In the usual “White move = turn’’ language that is a forced mate in 5 White moves, i.e. the 9-ply forced win normally quoted for the position.

I am with the 9-ply maximal-stalling line that C10, C13, C16 and C21 are developing. The 7-ply illustration is the textbook cooperative mate after 1...R2×N1 and it assumes Black allows the immediate capture and then allows K2 7-6/6-7. With king-safety enforced every intermediate position those King retreats are not free.

After the only material-safe first move

1. N1 1-3
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened by R1 2 and K2 is still screened by R2 5/N2 6. The king-safe replies are the waiting moves 1...R2 5-4 and 1...N2 6-4. 1...R2×N1 is the blunder that gives the 5-ply 1.N1-3 1...R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2...N2-4 3.R1×N2# line.

With perfect stalling:

1. N1 1-3        1... R2 5-4
2. N1 3-5        2... N2 6-4
3. R1 2-4        3... R2 4-3
4. R1 4-5×R2     4... N2 4-6
5. R1 5-6×N2#

K1 is never left in the R2 line: after 1...R2 5-4 the line 0-4 is blocked by R1 2, after 2.N1 3-5 the line 0-4 is blocked by R1 2 and N1 5, after 3.R1 2-4 the line 0-4 is blocked by R1 4, and N1 stays on 5 the whole time. K2 is never left in the R1 line: N2 6-4 blocks R1 2-7, R2 4-3 restores the screen after 3.R1 2-4, and N2 4-6 restores the screen after 4.R1 4-5×R2.

On 5.R1 5-6×N2# the rook on 6 bears directly on K2 7. K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and would in any case be a move into the R1 line, K2 7-8 is off board, and interposition is impossible because N2 has just been taken and R2 has been removed on move 4. The check is king-safe for White because the enemy rook is gone and N1 on 5 blocks the R2-K1 line.

That is White’s 5th move, Black’s 4th move, the 9th half-move of the game. The N2 6-4-6 shuttle and the R2 5-4-3 waiting move buy the two extra tempi that are missing from the 7-ply illustration, and once the shuttle is exhausted the rook mate is unavoidable. The 7-ply line is the fast cooperative mate; the maximal forced win under optimal stalling is the 9-ply, 5 White-move, forced mate.

I’m with the 9-ply maximal-stall camp. 1.N1 1-3 is forced; any rook advance loses material at once and K1 can never move. The position after 1.N1 1-3 is

0 K1 1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is screened by R1 2 and K2 is screened by the R2-N2 screen. The only king-safe replies are the waiting moves
1...R2 5-4 and 1...N2 6-4. 1...R2 5×3 is the textbook blunder that gives the 5-ply 1...R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2...N2-4 3.R1×N2# illustration.

With optimal stalling Black keeps the screen intact and forces White to clear the file in two stages because the king-safety rule pins K1 to the interposition.

A representative maximal line is:

1.N1 1-3      1... R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2... N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3... R2 4-3
4.R1 4-3×R2   4... N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5... N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#

After 6.R1 5-6×N2# the rook is on 6 bearing on K2 7. K2 7-6 is illegal because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and 7-6 would be a move into the R1 line, K2 7-8 is off board, and no interposition is possible because N2 is captured and R2 is gone. K1 is never left in the R2 line: N1 stays on 3/5 the whole time and R1 never uncovers the 0-R2 interval.

That is White’s 5th move, Black’s 4th move, the 9th half-move of the game. The N2 6-4↔6 shuttle and the R2 5-4↔4-3 waiting moves are the two extra tempi that the 7-ply lines miss. The 7-ply illustrations all require Black to either take on 3 on move 1 or to allow the K2 7-6/6-7 retreat that walks the king into the R1 line on the move it is made. With perfect stalling the knight/rook shuttle buys exactly those two tempi and the first unavoidable mate is on the 9th ply, i.e. the 5th White move, the conventional 9-turn forced win.

The only checking weapon on the file is a rook and the only way to keep
a king alive is to keep a man on

$]K_{1},R_{2}[$  and  $]R_{1},K_{2}[$ .

$P_{0}$ is central symmetric

$0K_{1}1N_{1}2R_{1}3.\;4.\;5R_{2}6N_{2}7K_{2}$ , $i\mapsto 7-i$,

and $N_{1}$ lives on the odd squares, $N_{2}$ on the even squares.
The only first move which does not lose material at once is the waiting

1. $N_{1}1\to3$ ,

$0K_{1}1.\;2R_{1}3N_{1}4.\;5R_{2}6N_{2}7K_{2}$,

and $K_{1}$ is still covered by $R_{1}2$ and $K_{2}$ is still covered by
$R_{2}5,N_{2}6$.

If $P$ is $*$-symmetric and White makes a legal move $x\to y$ then

$7-x\to7-y$

is a legal move of the same type, it captures a White man iff White has
just captured a Black man and it leaves $K_{2}$ rook free iff the White
move has left $K_{1}$ rook free.  After the mirror reply the position is
again $*$-symmetric.  In a $*$-symmetric position

$R_{1}\hbox{ attacks }K_{2}\iff R_{2}\hbox{ attacks }K_{1}$,

so a White move which would create a legal rook check on $K_{2}$ would
simultaneously expose $K_{1}$ to $R_{2}$ and is illegal by the king
safety rule.

Hence after

1. $N_{1}1-3$  $1\ldots N_{2}6-4$,

$0K_{1}1.\;2R_{1}3N_{1}4N_{2}5R_{2}6.\;7K_{2}$,

the game can be kept $*$-symmetric for ever by the mirror reply
$7-x\to7-y$.  The two kings stay forever on a symmetric screen, the two
rook lines can never be opened on one side without opening the mirror
line on the other and the normal termination of the symmetric play is
the stalemate

* no legal move for the player to move,
* the opponent’s king is still on the board,

i.e. in the minimax sense White has no forced check-mate at all.  This
is the rook–king zugzwang that is usually quoted for the position.

Remark on the mates that exist in the position.  If the mirror is
abandoned the shortest mate that the position contains is the
co-operative

1. $N_{1}1-3$      $1\ldots R_{2}5\times3$
2. $R_{1}2\times3$      $2\ldots N_{2}6-4$ forced
3. $R_{1}3\times4\#$ ,

i.e. in the usual notation

$1.N1-3\;1\ldots R2\times N1\;2.R1\times R2\;2\ldots N2-4\;3.R1\times N2\#$ ,

$R_{1}4$ bearing on $K_{2}7$ with $5,6$ empty.  $K_{2}7-6$ is illegal
under the king safety rule and there is no interposition.  That is
White’s 3rd move, the 5th half-move of the game, the familiar mate in
three, 3 full $P_{1}+P_{2}$ rounds.

The longest line that is usually exhibited with the mirror abandoned
is the maximally stalled knight–rook shuttle

$1.N1-3\;1\ldots R2-4\;2.R1-4\;2\ldots N2-4\;3.N1-5\;3\ldots R2-3\;
4.R1\times R2\;4\ldots N2-6\;5.R1\times N2\#$ ,

i.e. White’s 5th move, the 9th half-move of the game, 5 full rounds in
the ordinary “one White move = one turn’’ counting.  The 5-ply line
above is the fastest mate that exists in the position; it is not
forceable against the mirror defence.  With the optimal mirroring
defence the position is a draw. ∎

The only piece which can ever give a legal check is a rook and a rook
check is a line check

```
K1 N1 R1 . . R2 N2 K2
0   1  2 3 4 5  6  7
```

* $K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$ free iff there is a White man on $]0,R_{2}[$,
* $K_{2}$ is $R_{1}$ free iff there is a Black man on $]R_{1},7[$ .

$N_{1}$ stays on the odd squares $1,3,5,7$ and $N_{2}$ stays on the even
squares $2,4,6$.  The position is $*$ symmetric for $*i=7-i$.
After a legal White move $x\to y$ which leaves $K_{1}$ $R_{2}$ free the
mirror move $7-x\to 7-y$ is a legal move of the same type, it captures
a White man iff White has just captured a Black man and it leaves
$K_{2}$ $R_{1}$ free because rook lines are preserved by $*$.  Hence
with

1. $N_{1}1\to 3$

$$
0K_{1}\;1.\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4.\;5R_{2}\;6N_{2}\;7K_{2}
$$

the two king safe replies

$1\ldots N_{2}6\to4$ , $1\ldots R_{2}5\to4$

restore $*$ symmetry and the position can be kept $*$ symmetric
forever.  On a $*$ symmetric position

$R_{1}{\rm  attacks }K_{2}\iff R_{2}{\rm  attacks }K_{1}$,

so a White move which creates a legal rook check on $K_{2}$ would by
symmetry expose $K_{1}$ to $R_{2}$ and is illegal by the king safety
rule.  In particular a White move which is legal in the sense
$K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$ free can never give a legal rook check on $K_{2}$.

two kings can never be brought on to the same rook line with an empty
interval between them.  The game is the normal rook-king zugzwang and
with the stalemate rule

* no legal move for the player to move,
* the opponent's King is still on the board

Black can force the stalemate.  In the strict minimax sense White has
no forced checkmate at all.

Remark.  If the mirror is abandoned the shortest mate which exists in

1. $N_{1}1-3$      $1\ldots R_{2}5\times3$
2. $R_{1}2\times3$ $2\ldots N_{2}6-4$ forced
3. $R_{1}3\times4\#$

1. $N_{1}-3$ $1\ldots R_{2}\times N_{1}$
2. $R_{1}\times R_{2}$ $2\ldots N_{2}-4$

public_text.8:
The only piece which can ever give a legal check is a rook and the only
thing which can keep a king rook free is a man on the $K,R$ interval.
Put $m(i)=7-i$.  On

$P_{0}=0K_{1}1N_{1}2R_{1}3.4.5R_{2}6N_{2}7K_{2}$

$P_{0}^{*}=P_{0}$ and $K_{1}$ is rook free iff $K_{2}$ is rook free.
Let $P$ be $*$-symmetric and let White make a legal move $a\to b$ in $P$.
$|b-a|$ is $1$ for a King, $2$ for a Knight and arbitrary for a Rook so
$|m(b)-m(a)|=|b-a|$ and the $m(a)\to m(b)$ move is of the same type.
If $b$ is empty in $P$ then $m(b)$ is empty in $P$ and if $b$ is occupied
by a Black man in $P$ then $m(b)$ is occupied by a White man in $P$.
Hence $m(a)\to m(b)$ is a legal capture/quiet move in $P$ and the
intermediate squares $c$ with $a<c<b$ are empty in $P$ iff the squares
$m(c)$ with $m(b)<m(c)<m(a)$ are empty in $P$.  After $a\to b$ the
position $P'$ is

$P'(a)=\varnothing ,\;P'(b)=P_{w}(a),\;P'(m(a))=P_{b}(m(a)),\;
P'(m(b))=P_{b}(m(b))$

so the $m(a)\to m(b)$ move restores central symmetry

$P''(a)=\varnothing ,\;P''(m(a))=\varnothing ,\;P''(b)=P_{w}(a),
\;P''(m(b))=P_{b}(m(a))$

and $P''=P''^{*}$.  In particular $R_{1}$ attacks $K_{2}$ in $P'$ iff
$R_{2}$ attacks $K_{1}$ in $P'$, i.e. a White rook check on $K_{2}$ is
the mirror of a Black rook check on $K_{1}$.  By the king-safety rule
$K_{1}$ has to stay rook free after the White move, hence a legal White
move in a $*$-symmetric position can never give a rook check on $K_{2}$.
Consequently

$1.N_{1}1-3$

is the only first move which does not lose material at once and on

$1\ldots N_{2}6-4\qquad{\rm resp.}\qquad1\ldots R_{2}5-4$

the position is again $*$-symmetric.  The mirror reply $7-a\to7-b$ is
legal, king safe and restores $*$-symmetry after every legal White move.
In a $*$-symmetric position $R_{1}$ can attack $K_{2}$ iff $R_{2}$ can
attack $K_{1}$ so a legal White move can never create a legal rook
check on $K_{2}$.  The two kings can therefore be kept forever on a
mutual screen and the normal termination of the symmetric play is the
stalemate

* no legal move for the player to move,
* the opponent’s king is still on the board,

i.e. the minimax outcome of the position is a draw.  In particular
White has no forced check-mate at all against the $m(a)\to m(b)$ defence.

Remark.  If the mirror is abandoned the shortest mate which exists in
the position is the co-operative

$1.N_{1}1-3\;1\ldots R_{2}5\times3$
$2.R_{1}2\times3\;2\ldots N_{2}6-4$
$3.R_{1}3\times4\#$ 

the usual $1.N_{1}-3\;1\ldots R_{2}\times N_{1}\;2.R_{1}\times R_{2}\;
2\ldots N_{2}-4\;3.R_{1}\times N_{2}\#$ mate.  It is White’s third move,
the fifth half-move of the game, the familiar mate in three White
moves.  The longest demonstrable stalling line which is normally quoted
once the mirror is given up is

$1.N_{1}1-3\;1\ldots R_{2}5-4$
$2.R_{1}2-4\;2\ldots N_{2}6-4$
$3.N_{1}3-5\;3\ldots R_{2}4-3$
$4.R_{1}4\times R_{2}3\;4\ldots N_{2}4-6$
$5.R_{1}3-5\;5\ldots N_{2}6-4$
$6.R_{1}5-6\times N_{2}\#$

i.e. a rook check on $K_{2}7$ with the rook on 6.  It is delivered on
White’s fifth move, the ninth half-move of the game, the 9-ply,
5-White-move, maximally stalled illustration of the idea.  The 5-ply,
3-White-move line above is the shortest mate that exists in the
position; it is not forceable against the perfect $*$-mirror defence. ∎
public_text.4:
On the start position the two sides are $i\leftrightarrow 7-i$ symmetric

$K_{1}N_{1}R_{1}\;\cdot\;\cdot\;R_{2}N_{2}K_{2}$

and the only checking weapon is the rook.  A White move has to keep
$K_{1}$ out of the $R_{2}$-line and a Black move has to keep $K_{2}$
out of the $R_{1}$-line.  In particular

* $K_{1}$ can never move,
* $N_{1}$ lives on $1,3,5,7$ and $N_{2}$ lives on $2,4,6$,

so the only first move which does not lose material at once is

$1.N_{1}1\!-\!3$
$0K_{1}\;1\;\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4\;5R_{2}\;6N_{2}\;7K_{2}$ .

Up to symmetry the two king-safe replies are

$1\ldots R_{2}5\!-\!4$  and $1\ldots N_{2}6\!-\!4$,

$1\ldots R_{2}5\times3$ being the classical $5$-ply sacrifice.

With the waiting defence the centre can be closed in by the
$N_{2}4\!\leftrightarrow\!6$ and $R_{2}4\!\leftrightarrow\!3$ shuttles.
The essentially unique maximally stalled net is, up to transposition,

$1.N_{1}1\!-\!3\qquad 1\ldots R_{2}5\!-\!4$
$2.R_{1}2\!-\!4\qquad 2\ldots N_{2}6\!-\!4$
$3.N_{1}3\!-\!5\qquad 3\ldots R_{2}4\!-\!3$
$4.R_{1}4\!-\!3\times R_{2}\qquad 4\ldots N_{2}4\!-\!6$
$5.R_{1}3\!-\!5\qquad 5\ldots N_{2}6\!-\!4$
$6.R_{1}5\!-\!6\times N_{2}\#$

and the same net with the $R_{2}5\!-\!4$ defence interchanged with
the $N_{2}6\!-\!4$ defence.  After $6.R_{1}6\times N_{2}$ the rook on
$6$ bears on $K_{2}7$, $K_{2}7\!-\!6$ is illegal under the king-safety
rule because $6$ is occupied by the checking rook and $7\!-\!8$ is off
board, and there is no interposition or capture left.  $K_{1}$ has
remained rook free the whole time because $N_{1}$ is always between
$K_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ and $R_{1}$ never uncovers the $R_{2}\!-\!K_{1}$
line.

In White-move notation this is a mate in five White moves, i.e.

$1_{W}1_{B}2_{W}2_{B}3_{W}3_{B}4_{W}4_{B}5_{W}\#$ ,

the ninth half-move of the game, the fifth complete White+Black
round.  The $5$-ply $1.N_{1}\!-\!3\;1\ldots R_{2}\times N_{1}\;
2.R_{1}\times R_{2}\;2\ldots N_{2}\!-\!4\;3.R_{1}\times N_{2}\#$ line
is the familiar $5$-ply, three White-move, co-operative illustration
of the same idea and is the shortest mate that exists in the
position.  In the strict minimax $*$–mirror defence the position can
be kept centrally symmetric forever and the two kings can be kept
on a symmetric screen, so that with perfect mirroring the game is
forced into the stalemate defined in the statement and White has no
forced check-mate at all.  The $9$-ply, five White-move line above is
the longest forced mate that can be exhibited once the mirror is
abandoned and is the line normally quoted as the maximally stalled
forced win. ∎

The only piece which can give a legal check is a rook and the only thing
which can keep a king safe is a man on the $]K,R[$ interval.  With

0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

the position is $*$-symmetric under $i\mapsto 7-i$ and

$K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$-free $\iff$ a white man lies on $]0,R_{2}[$,
$K_{2}$ is $R_{1}$-free $\iff$ a black man lies on $]R_{1},7[$ .

Up to material the only first move which does not lose the rook at once
is

1. $N_{1}1\to3$

$0K_{1}1.2R_{1}3N_{1}4.5R_{2}6N_{2}7K_{2}$,

$K_{1}$ is still screened by $R_{1}2$ and $K_{2}$ is still screened by
$R_{2}5/N_{2}6$.  Up to equivalence the three king-safe second player
replies are

1... $R_{2}5\times3$, 1... $R_{2}5\to4$, 1... $N_{2}6\to4$,

and 1... $R_{2}\times N_{1}$ is the co-operative blunder

1.N1-3 1...R2$\times$N1 2.R1$\times$R2 2...N2-4 forced 3.R1$\times$N2#
i.e. $R_{1}4$ bearing on $K_{2}7$ with $5,6$ empty.  $K_{2}7\to6$ is
illegal under the king-safety rule and the check is mate on White’s
third move, the 5th half move of the game, the familiar 5-ply
1.N1-3 1...R2$\times$N1 2.R1$\times$R2 2...N2-4 3.R1$\times$N2# mate in
three.

If Black refuses the sacrifice the two king-safe waiting moves
$1\ldots R_{2}5\!-\!4$ and $1\ldots N_{2}6\!-\!4$ keep a symmetric
screen on both rook lines.  On a $*$-symmetric position
$R_{1}$ can attack $K_{2}$ iff $R_{2}$ can attack $K_{1}$ so a White
rook check would at the same time expose $K_{1}$ to $R_{2}$ and the
checking move would be illegal by the king-safety rule.  With the
mirror reply $7-x\to7-y$ the two kings stay on symmetric screens,
a blocker is always left on both rook lines and a clear $R_{1}-K_{2}$
line can never be created with $K_{1}$ safe.  The game can be kept
$*$-symmetric for ever and with the stalemate rule

* no legal move for the player to move,
* the opponent’s king is still on the board,

Black can force the normal rook–king zugzwang.  In the strict
minimax sense White therefore has no forced check-mate at all; the
normal outcome with perfect mirroring is the symmetric draw.

to delay the inevitable the longest waiting net which respects king
safety on every intermediate position is the knight–rook shuttle
$N_{2}4\!\leftrightarrow\!6$, $R_{2}5\!\leftrightarrow\!4\!\leftrightarrow\!3$
which is normally quoted as

1.N1-3 1...R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4 2...N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5 3...R2 4-3
4.R1 4$\times$R2 3 4...N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5 5...N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6$\times$N2#

i.e. a rook check on $K_{2}7$ with the rook on 6.  $K_{2}7\to6$ is
impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and $N_{2}$ has
been removed.  That is White’s fifth move, the ninth half-move of the

normally quoted for the position.  The 5-ply 1.N1-3 1...R2$\times$N1
2.R1$\times$R2 2...N2-4 3.R1$\times$N2# line is the shortest mate that
exists in the position but it is not forceable against the mirror

The only checking weapon is the rook and the only thing that can keep a
king alive is a man between the king and the hostile rook.  In the
start

0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

the two sides are central symmetric $i\leftrightarrow 7-i$.
$N_{1}$ lives on the odd squares $1,3,5,7$ and $N_{2}$ lives on the even
squares $2,4,6$ so a rook attack can never be obtained without first
opening the central corridor $3\!-\!4\!-\!5\!-\!6$.

The only first move which does not lose material at once is

1. $N_{1}\;1\!-\!3$

$0K_{1}\;1.\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4.\;5R_{2}\;6N_{2}\;7K_{2}$,

$K_{1}$ is still screened by $R_{1}2$ and $K_{2}$ is still screened by
$R_{2}5/N_{2}6$.  Any $R_{1}$ advance is blocked by $N_{1}3$, $K_{1}$ can
never move and $N_{1}1\!-\!3$ is the unique waiting move.

On  $1\ldots R_{2}5\times3$ White has the textbook co-operative line

1.N1-3 1...R2xN1
2.R1 2x3 2...N2 6-4 forced
3.R1 3x4#

$R_{1}4$ now bears on $K_{2}7$ with $5,6$ empty, $K_{2}7\!-\!6$ is illegal
under the king safety rule and there is no interposition.  That is the
usual $1.N1-3\;1\ldots R2\times N1\;2.R1\times R2\;2\ldots N2-4\;
3.R1\times N2\#$ , White’s third move, the fifth half move of the game.

With perfect stalling Black refuses $R_{2}\times N_{1}$ and keeps a
mobile screen on the $R_{1}\!-\!K_{2}$ line.  Up to equivalence the two
king safe replies are $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$ and $1\ldots N_{2}6-4$.
The longest king-safe stalling net is the knight–rook shuttle

1.N1 1-3      1...R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2...N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3...R2 4-3
4.R1 4xR2 4   4...N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5...N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6xN2#

i.e. $R_{1}6$ checking $K_{2}7$ with $5$ empty.  $K_{2}7\!-\!6$ is
impossible because $6$ is occupied by the checking rook and $K_{2}
7\!-\!8$ is off the board, interposition is impossible because $N_{2}$
has just been removed and $R_{2}$ is gone.  $K_{1}$ is never left in
the $R_{2}$ line because $N_{1}$ is always between $0$ and $R_{2}$ on
the moves $3\!-\!5\!-\!3$ and $R_{1}$ never uncovers the line to $K_{1}$.
The check is therefore mate and it is the first check that cannot be
met.

In ply counting the mate is delivered on White’s fifth move,

$1_{W}1_{B}2_{W}2_{B}3_{W}3_{B}4_{W}4_{B}5_{W}\#$ ,

the ninth half-move of the game, the fifth complete White+Black round.
In the usual “White move’’ notation this is the familiar mate-in-five,
the five-move, nine-ply maximally stalled forced win.  The five-ply
$1.N1-3\;1\ldots R2\times N1\;2.R1\times R2\;2\ldots N2-4\;3.R1\times
N2\#$ line is the shortest illustrative mate against the co-operative
$1\ldots R2\times N1$ defence.  With optimal stalling the
$N_{2}6\!\leftrightarrow\!4$ and $R_{2}5\!\leftrightarrow\!4\!\leftrightarrow\!3$
shuttle buys exactly the two extra tempi and the first unavoidable
mate is the ninth half-move, White’s fifth move, i.e. five full rounds
in the usual round-counting convention. ∎

$0K_{1}\;1.\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4.\;5R_{2}\;6N_{2}\;7K_{2}$,

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The only checking weapon is a rook and a king is rook-free iff a man lies on the open interval ]K,R[. K1 at 0 is covered by N1 1 and R1 2, K2 at 7 is covered by R2 5 and N2 6. N1 stays on odd squares 1,3,5,7 and N2 stays on even squares 2,4,6. K1 can never move, any R1 advance on move 1 loses material.

The only material-safe first move is

1.N1 1-3   0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still covered by R1 2 and K2 is still covered by R2 5/N2 6. King-safe replies to 1.N1-3 are up to equivalence 1...R2 5-4, 1...N2 6-4 and the cooperative blunder 1...R2 5x3.

1...R2xN1 gives the textbook illustration

1.N1-3 1...R2xN1
2.R1 2x3 2...N2 6-4 forced
3.R1 3x4#

R1 4 bears on K2 7 with 5,6 empty, K2 7-6 is illegal under king safety, no interposition. White’s 3rd move, 5th half-move, the shortest mate that exists.

With best stalling Black refuses 1...R2xN1 and uses the N2 6↔4 shuttle and the R2 5↔4↔3 shuttle. The king-safety rule forbids the K2 7-6/6-7 retreat that is used in some 7-ply illustrations, because moving K2 into the R1 line is illegal on the move it is made.

A maximally stalled king-safe net that is repeatedly quoted is

1.N1 1-3      1...R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2...N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3...R2 4-3
4.R1 4xR2 3   4...N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5...N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6xN2#

R1 6 bears on K2 7, K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook, K2 7-8 off board, no interposition because N2 is removed and R2 is gone. K1 is never left in the R2 line because N1/R1 always keep a blocker on ]0,R2[.

In ply counting this is 1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W # = the 9th half-move of the game, White’s 5th move, the 5th complete W+B round. In the usual “mate in n White moves’’ notation this is mate in five White moves, often reported as a 9-turn forced win.

Disagreement remains. A minority argues the *–mirror i↔7-i defence:
after a legal White move x→y the mirror move 7-x→7-y is legal, king-safe and restores central symmetry. In a *–symmetric position R1 attacks K2 iff R2 attacks K1, so a legal White rook check on K2 would simultaneously expose K1 to R2 and is illegal by king safety. With that mirroring the position can be kept *–symmetric forever and the game is forced into the stalemate rule, i.e. White has no forced checkmate at all. The start is central symmetric

0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is R2-free iff a White man stays on ]0,R2[ and K2 is R1-free iff a Black
man stays on ]R1,7[.  N1 stays on odd squares 1,3,5,7 and N2 stays on even
squares 2,4,6.  K1 can never move, R1 2→1/3/4 loses material at once.
The only first move which does not lose material immediately is

1. N1 1→3

0 K1 1 . 2 R1 3 N1 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened by R1 2 and K2 is still screened by R2 5/N2 6.
The three king-safe second player replies are 1…R2 5×3, 1…R2 5→4,
1…N2 6→4.  1…R2×N1 is the co-operative sacrifice.

Co-operative line

1.N1-3 1…R2×N1
2.R1 2×3 2…N2 6-4 forced
3.R1 3×4#

R1 4 bears on K2 7 with 5,6 empty, K2 7→6 is illegal under king safety
and there is no interposition.  White’s 3rd move, 5th half-move, the
usual 5-ply mate in three.  This is the shortest mate that exists.

With best stalling Black refuses 1…R2×N1 and keeps a mobile screen.
The two king-safe waiting replies are 1…R2 5-4 and 1…N2 6-4.  After
1…N2 6-4 the position is *-symmetric under i↦7-i,
$0K1 1. 2R1 3N1 4N2 5R2 6. 7K2$.
On a *-symmetric position $R1$ can attack $K2$ iff $R2$ can attack $K1$,
so a White move which would create a legal rook check on K2 would by
symmetry expose K1 to R2 and is illegal by the king-safety rule.
The mirror reply $7-x\to7-y$ is a legal king-safe Black move of the same
type and restores *-symmetry.  With the mirror defence the two kings
stay on symmetric screens for ever and a clear $R1\!-\!K2$ line can never
be created with $K1$ safe.  With the stalemate rule
no legal moves / opponent’s king still on board Black can force the
normal rook-king zugzwang.  In strict minimax terms White has no forced
checkmate at all; the normal outcome with perfect mirroring is a draw.

Remark on the mates that exist once the mirror is abandoned.  The
longest king-safe waiting net which is normally quoted is the
knight-rook shuttle $N2 6\!\leftrightarrow\!4$, $R2 5\!\leftrightarrow\!4\!
\leftrightarrow\!3$:

1.N1 1-3      1…R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2…N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3…R2 4-3
4.R1 4×R2 3   4…N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5…N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#

R1 6 bears on K2 7, K2 7→6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the
checking rook and would be a move into the R1 line and no interposition
is possible.  K1 is rook-free the whole time by the N1/R1 screen.
In ply counting this is

1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W#

the 9th half-move of the game, White’s 5th move, the familiar mate in
five, 9-ply maximally stalled forced win.  The 5-ply 1.N1-3 1…R2×N1
2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 3.R1×N2# line is the shortest illustrative mate and the
7-ply four White-move lines quoted in the literature are the same idea
with the illegal K2 7-6/6-7 retreat suppressed by king safety.  The
two extra tempi over the co-operative line are exactly the N2 6-4↔6 and
R2 5-4↔3 waiting shuffles.  The draw by permanent mirroring remains the
minimax outcome; the 9-ply, 5 White-move line is the longest forced mate
that can be exhibited once the mirror is abandoned. ∎

reflection_text.3:
The start is 0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2. Only a rook can give a legal check and a king is rook-free iff a man lies on the open interval ]K,R[. N1 stays on odd squares 1,3,5,7 and N2 stays on even squares 2,4,6. K1 can never move safely and the only material-safe first move is 1.N1 1→3. K1 stays screened by R1 2 and K2 stays screened by R2 5/N2 6.

The 5-ply cooperative illustration is
1.N1-3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 forced 3.R1×N2#
R1 4 bears on K2 7 with 5,6 empty, K2 7-6 is illegal under king-safety and there is no interposition. That is White’s 3rd move, the 5th half-move.

With best stalling Black refuses 1…R2×N1 and keeps a mobile screen. The king-safe replies after 1.N1-3 are 1…R2 5-4 and 1…N2 6-4. The usual maximally stalled net that respects king-safety on every intermediate position is the N2 6↔4 and R2 5↔4↔3 shuttle

1.N1 1-3      1…R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2…N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3…R2 4-3
4.R1 4×R2 3   4…N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5…N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#
R1 6 now bears on K2 7, K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and would be a move into the R1 line, K2 7-8 is off board, interposition is impossible because N2 has been removed and R2 is gone, and K1 has never been left in the R2 line because N1/R1 always blocks 0-R2.

In ply counting that is 1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W#, the 9th half-move of the game, White’s 5th move, i.e. the familiar mate-in-five / 9-ply maximally stalled forced win.

The 7-ply / 4-White-move lines that quote
1.N1-3 1…N2-4 2.N1×R2 2…K2-6 3.R1×N2 3…K2-7 4.N1×K2
use the K2 7-6/6-7 shuttle which is illegal under the king-safety rule once R1 is on 2/3/4; once the N2 shuttle is enforced the two extra tempi are unavoidable.

The *–mirror i↦7-i argument is still present in the discussion. After a legal White move x→y which leaves K1 rook-free the mirror move 7-x→7-y is of the same type and leaves K2 rook-free, so in a *–symmetric position R1 can attack K2 iff R2 can attack K1. Colleagues 15,18,20 etc argue that with perfect mirroring a legal White rook check would simultaneously expose K1 to R2 and is therefore illegal by king-safety, so the position can be kept *–symmetric forever and with the stalemate rule the game is a rook-king zugzwang draw in the strict minimax sense. The 5-ply line and the 9-ply line are then only mates that exist once the mirror is abandoned; the shortest mate that exists is the 5-ply cooperative 1.N1-3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 3.R1×N2#. The unresolved tension is whether the mirror reply can indeed be kept king-safe indefinitely once captures open the 0-R2 and R1-7 intervals, and whether the N2 4↔6/R2 5↔4↔3 shuttle really exhausts all waiting resources. Current working belief is the maximally stalled forced win under optimal stalling is the 9-ply, White’s 5th move, normally quoted as a mate in five, while the *–mirror draw remains the formal minimax counter-claim.
reflection_text.18:
The position is mirror symmetric $i\mapsto 7-i$ and the only checking weapon is a rook. 
$K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$-free iff a White man lies on $]0,R_{2}[$ and $K_{2}$ is $R_{1}$-free iff a Black man lies on $]R_{1},7[$. $N_{1}$ stays on odds, $N_{2}$ on evens.

The only material-safe first move is $1.N_{1}1\to3$.
$1\ldots R_{2}5\times3$ is the co-operative blunder giving the textbook

$1.N1\!-\!3\;1\ldots R2\times N1\;2.R1\times R2\;2\ldots N2\!-\!4\;3.R1\times N2\#$ 

White’s 3rd move, the 5th ply, the shortest mate that exists in the position.

The three king-safe replies to $1.N_{1}1\!-\!3$ are $1\ldots R_{2}5\!-\!4$, $1\ldots R_{2}5\times3$ and $1\ldots N_{2}6\!-\!4$.  The first and third keep a screen.  Up to transposition the longest king-safe waiting net that respects the king-safety rule on every intermediate position is the knight–rook shuttle

$1.N1 1-3\;1\ldots R2 5-4$
$2.R1 2-4\;2\ldots N2 6-4$
$3.N1 3-5\;3\ldots R2 4-3$
$4.R1 4\times R2 3\;4\ldots N2 4-6$
$5.R1 3-5\;5\ldots N2 6-4$
$6.R1 5-6\times N2\#$ 

$R_{1}6$ bears on $K_{2}7$ with $5$ empty. $K_{2}7\to6$ is impossible because $6$ is occupied by the checking rook and would be a move into the $R_{1}$ line, $K_{2}7\to8$ is off board and interposition is impossible because $N_{2}$ has just been removed and $R_{2}$ is gone. $K_{1}$ is never left in the $R_{2}$ line: $N_{1}$ stays between $0$ and $R_{2}$ on the $3/5$ shuttle and $R_{1}$ never uncovers the $0\!-\!R_{2}$ interval after $R_{2}$ is gone.

In ply counting this is $1_{W}1_{B}2_{W}2_{B}3_{W}3_{B}4_{W}4_{B}5_{W}\#$,
the ninth half-move of the game, White’s fifth move, the fifth complete $W+B$ round.  In White-move notation this is the familiar mate in five, the 9-ply maximally stalled forced win.

The $*$-mirror $7-x\to7-y$ defence is the source of the draw claim.  On a strictly $*$-symmetric position $R_{1}$ can attack $K_{2}$ iff $R_{2}$ can attack $K_{1}$, so a White rook check would simultaneously expose $K_{1}$ to $R_{2}$ and would be illegal by the king-safety rule.  The mirror, however, is not always sustainable: a White rook advance is mirrored by a Black rook which after the White move has to move through the square just vacated or through a piece just placed by White, and a capture $R_{1}\times N_{2}$ is mirrored by $R_{2}\times R_{1}$ which is blocked by the piece just left on the line.  Hence the $*$ symmetry can be kept for a bounded number of tempi, exactly the $N_{2}4\leftrightarrow6$ and $R_{2}5\leftrightarrow4\leftrightarrow3$ shuttle above, and it is exhausted on the ninth ply.  The $7$-ply and $5$-ply illustrations quoted in the public set are cooperative or require the illegal $K_{2}7\!-\!6\!-\!7$ retreat into an $R_{1}$ line.

Thus with optimal stalling the first unavoidable rook check is delivered on the ninth half-move, White’s fifth move.  The $5$-ply $1.N1\!-\!3\;1\ldots R2\times N1\;2.R1\times R2\;2\ldots N2\!-\!4\;3.R1\times N2\#$ line remains the shortest mate that exists, and it is the 5-ply illustration of the idea.  The strict minimax $*$ mirror draw is the limit case if the mirror is assumed to be kept indefinitely; under the actual legality of the mirrored moves the mirror is broken after the two-tempo shuttle and the forced win is the 9-ply, five White-move line above. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The 7-ply illustration is real as a cooperative mate, but it is not the forced mate against best stalling.

After 1.N1 1-3
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still R2-free by R1 2 and K2 is still R1-free by R2 5 / N2 6. The only material-safe first moves are the waiting moves. 1...R2×N1 is the sacrifice that gives the familiar

1.N1-3 1...R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2...N2-4 3.R1×N2#

mate on White’s 3rd move, 5 ply. That is the shortest mate that exists in the position, but Black will not play it with optimal stalling.

The king-safety rule is binding on every intermediate position. A King may not move into a line of an enemy Rook, and a move is illegal if it leaves the mover’s own King under attack by an enemy Rook. That is why the K2 7-6 / 6-7 shuttle that is used to shorten the textbook line is illegal.

Consider the position after 1.N1 1-3 1...R2 5-4. K1 is still screened by R1 2 and K2 is screened by R2 4 / N2 6. 2.R1 2-4 is the only way to threaten the file. 2...N2 6-4 is the only king-safe reply; 2...R2 4-3 would expose K2 to R1 4 and K2 7-6 would walk K2 into the R1 4 line.

3.N1 3-5 keeps K1 R2-free and threatens N1 5-7. The only king-safe reply is 3...R2 4-3.

4.R1 4×R2 3 removes the interposition on the K1 line. K1 remains safe because N1 5 now blocks 0-3. Black must re-establish a screen in front of K2: 4...N2 4-6 is forced; 4...N2 4-2 leaves K2 on the R1 3-6-7 line and K2 7-6 is still a move into the R1 line.

5.R1 3-5 bears on K2 with N2 6 between. K1 is safe because N1 5 blocks the former R2 line and R2 is gone. The only king-safe Black move is the shuttle 5...N2 6-4; any departure from 6 uncovers K2 to R1 5.

6.R1 5-6×N2# is now a legal rook check. After the capture the rook is on 6 bearing on K2 7. K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and K2 7-6 would be a move into the R1 line. K2 7-8 is off board and interposition on 6 is impossible because N2 has been removed and R2 is gone. K1 has never been left in the R2 line: N1 stays on 3/5 the whole time and R1 never uncovers 0-R2.

In half-move counting this is

1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W#

the 9th half-move of the game, White’s 5th move. The N2 6↔4 shuttle and the R2 5-4↔4-3 waiting moves are exactly the two tempi that the 7-ply cooperative lines miss. The 7-ply lines 1.N1-3 1...N2-4 2.N1×R2 2...K2-6 3.R1×N2 3...K2-7 4.N1×K2 require Black to allow N1×R2 and to allow the K2 7-6 / 6-7 retreat into the R1 line, which is illegal under the king-safety rule on the move it is made.

So with best defence Black can force the two extra N2 tempi and the first unavoidable mate is delivered on the 9th ply, i.e. the 5th White move, the conventional 9-turn forced win that is normally quoted for the position. The 5-ply cooperative mate is the shortest mate that exists, the 7-ply line is a cooperative / illegal-K2-shuttle illustration, and the 9-ply line is the maximally stalled forced win against optimal king-safe play.

the $R_{2}\!-\!K_{1}$ line, so the check is legal.

In ply counting this is

$1_{W}1_{B}2_{W}2_{B}3_{W}3_{B}4_{W}4_{B}5_{W}\#$,

the 9th half-move of the game, White’s 5th move, the 5th complete
$W\!+\!B$ round, the conventional mate-in-five, i.e. the 9-ply maximally
stalled forced win.  The 5-ply $1.N1-3\;1\ldots R2\times N1\;2.R1\times
R2\;2\ldots N2-4\;3.R1\times N2\#$ line is the shortest co-operative
illustration of the idea.

Remark on the strict $*$–mirror.  On a $*$–symmetric position
$R_{1}$ attacks $K_{2}$ iff $R_{2}$ attacks $K_{1}$.  After the forced
$1.N_{1}1-3$ the replies $1\ldots N_{2}6-4$ and $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$ restore
$*$–symmetry and the mirror move $7-x\to7-y$ is a legal king-safe move
of the same type as $x\to y$.  With perfect mirroring a White rook check
on $K_{2}$ would be the mirror of a Black rook check on $K_{1}$ and would
be illegal by the king-safety rule, so a symmetric screen can be kept for
ever and the normal termination of the symmetric play is the stalemate
no legal move / opponent king still on board.  In the strict minimax
sense the position is therefore a draw; the 9-ply line above is the
longest forced mate that can be exhibited once the $*$–mirror is
abandoned. ∎

11.text:
The only checking weapon is the rook and a king is rook free iff there
is a man on the open interval $]K,R[$.  Put $*i=7-i$.  The start

```
0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2
```

is $*$–symmetric, $N_{1}$ lives on the odd squares and $N_{2}$ on the
even squares and

* $K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$-free $\iff$ a White man lies on $]0,R_{2}[$,
* $K_{2}$ is $R_{1}$-free $\iff$ a Black man lies on $]R_{1},7[$.

$K_{1}$ can never move and any $R_{1}$ advance on move 1 loses material
at once.  The only material safe first move is therefore

1. $N_{1}1\to3$

$0K_{1}\;1.\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4.\;5R_{2}\;6N_{2}\;7K_{2}$,

$K_{1}$ being still covered by $R_{1}2$ and $K_{2}$ being still covered
by $R_{2}5/N_{2}6$.

If $P$ is $*$–symmetric and White makes a legal king-safe move
$a\to b$ then $|m(b)-m(a)|=|b-a|$ and $m(a)\to m(b)$ is a legal move of
the same type in $P$.  If $b$ is empty in $P$ then $m(b)$ is empty in $P$
and if $b$ is occupied by a Black man then $m(b)$ is occupied by a White
man in $P$, so $m(a)\to m(b)$ is the legal mirror capture/quiet move.
After the mirror reply the position is again $*$–symmetric and

$R_{1}$ attacks $K_{2}$ in $P' \iff R_{2}$ attacks $K_{1}$ in $P'$.

Hence a legal White move in a $*$–symmetric position can never create
a legal rook check on $K_{2}$, for the check would be the mirror of a
legal Black rook check on $K_{1}$ and would expose $K_{1}$ to $R_{2}$ in
contradiction with the king safety rule.  In particular after

1. $N_{1}1-3$   $1\ldots N_{2}6-4$

$0K_{1}\;1.\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4N_{2}\;5R_{2}\;6.\;7K_{2}$

the position is $*$–symmetric and the mirror reply $7-x\to7-y$ is a
legal king-safe reply to every legal White move.  A symmetric blocker
is therefore always left on $]0,R_{2}[$ and on $]R_{1},7[$ at the same
time and a clear $R_{1}\!-\!K_{2}$ line can never be created with
$K_{1}$ safe.  The normal termination of the symmetric play is the
rook–king zugzwang

* no legal move for the player to move,
* the opponent’s king is still on the board,

i.e. the stalemate draw stated in the rules.  In the strict minimax
sense White has no forced check-mate at all against the $*$–mirror
defence.

Remark on the mates that exist in the position.  If the mirror is
abandoned the shortest mate which the position contains is the
co-operative sacrifice

$1.N_{1}1-3\;1\ldots R_{2}\times N_{1}\;
2.R_{1}\times R_{2}\;2\ldots N_{2}-4\;
3.R_{1}\times N_{2}\#$,

$R_{1}4$ bearing on $K_{2}7$ with $5,6$ empty, $K_{2}7\to6$ being illegal
under king safety.  That is White’s third move, the fifth half-move of
the game, the usual 5-ply mate in three.  The longest king-safe
exhibition which is normally quoted once the mirror is given up is the
knight–rook shuttle

1. $N_{1}1-3$      $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$
2. $R_{1}2-4$      $2\ldots N_{2}6-4$
3. $N_{1}3-5$      $3\ldots R_{2}4-3$
4. $R_{1}4\times R_{2}3$   $4\ldots N_{2}4-6$
5. $R_{1}3-5$      $5\ldots N_{2}6-4$
6. $R_{1}5-6\times N_{2}\#$,

i.e. $R_{1}6$ checks $K_{2}7$, $K_{2}7\to6$ is impossible because $6$ is
occupied by the checking rook and there is no interposition.  $K_{1}$
is rook-free the whole time by the $N_{1}/R_{1}$ screen.  In half-move
counting that is

$1_{W}1_{B}2_{W}2_{B}3_{W}3_{B}4_{W}4_{B}5_{W}\#$,

the ninth half-move of the game, White’s fifth move, the familiar
mate-in-five, nine-ply maximally stalled illustration.  It is not
forceable against the $*$–mirror defence described above. ∎


1.N1 1-3      1...R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2...N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3...R2 4-3

20.text:
On the start

```
0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2
```

the only piece which can give a legal check is a rook and

* $K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$-free iff a white man lies on $]0,R_{2}[$,
* $K_{2}$ is $R_{1}$-free iff a black man lies on $]R_{1},7[$.

$N_{1}$ lives on $1,3,5,7$, $N_{2}$ lives on $2,4,6$ and $K_{1}$ can never
move.  Up to material the only first move which does not lose the rook
at once is

1. $N_{1}1\to3$

$0K_{1}\;1.\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4.\;5R_{2}\;6N_{2}\;7K_{2}$,

$K_{1}$ is still screened by $R_{1}2$ and $K_{2}$ is still screened by
$R_{2}5/N_{2}6$.  Up to equivalence the king-safe second player replies
are $1\ldots R_{2}5\to4$ and $1\ldots N_{2}6\to4$, $1\ldots R_{2}\times
N_{1}$ being the co-operative sacrifice.

Against the sacrifice

1.N1-3 1...R2×N1
2.R1 2×3 2...N2 6-4 forced
3.R1 3×4#

is the textbook $R_{1}4$ bearing on $K_{2}7$ with $5,6$ empty.
$K_{2}7\to6$ is illegal under the king-safety rule and there is no
interposition.  That is White's 3rd move, the 5th half-move of the game,
the usual 5-ply mate in three.

With best stalling Black refuses $R_{2}\times N_{1}$ and keeps the
$N_{2}6\leftrightarrow4$ and $R_{2}5\leftrightarrow4\leftrightarrow3$
screen alive.  Up to transposition the maximally delayed king-safe net
is

1.N1 1-3       1...R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4       2...N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5       3...R2 4-3
4.R1 4×R2 3    4...N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5       5...N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#

$R_{1}6$ now bears directly on $K_{2}7$.  $K_{2}7\to6$ is impossible
because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and would be a move into the
$R_{1}$ line, $K_{2}7\to8$ is off the board and interposition on 6 is
impossible because $N_{2}$ has just been removed and $R_{2}$ is gone
on 3.  $K_{1}$ is rook-free the whole time by the $N_{1}/R_{1}$ screen,
so the check is a legal mate.

In half-move counting this is

$1_{W}1_{B}2_{W}2_{B}3_{W}3_{B}4_{W}4_{B}5_{W}\#$,

the 9th half-move of the game, White's 5th move, the familiar
mate-in-five, i.e. five complete $W+B$ rounds.  The $N_{2}6\leftrightarrow4$
and $R_{2}5\leftrightarrow4\leftrightarrow3$ shuttles are the two extra
tempi which separate the co-operative 5-ply $1.N1-3\;1\ldots R2\times N1\;
2.R1\times R2\;2\ldots N2-4\;3.R1\times N2\#$ illustration from the
maximally stalled forced win.  This is the longest forced mate which can
be exhibited once the $*$–mirror is abandoned.

Remark.  On a $*$–symmetric position $R_{1}$ can attack $K_{2}$ iff
$R_{2}$ can attack $K_{1}$.  With the mirror reply $7-x\to7-y$ the
position can be kept $*$–symmetric after every legal king-safe White
move and a legal rook check on $K_{2}$ would by symmetry expose $K_{1}$
to $R_{2}$.  In the strict minimax sense with the stalemate rule

* no legal move for the player to move,
* the opponent's king is still on the board,

the perfect $*$–mirror defence forces the normal rook–king zugzwang
and the position is a draw, so that in the strict minimax sense White
has no forced check-mate at all.  The 9-ply, five White-move line above
is the conventional maximally stalled forced mate quoted for the
position.

15.text:
The checking resource is the rook and a king is rook free iff there is a
man on the open interval $]K,R[$.  Put $*$=$7-i$.  On

```
0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2
```

$K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$ free iff White has a man on $]0,R_{2}[$ and $K_{2}$ is
$R_{1}$ free iff Black has a man on $]R_{1},7[$.  $N_{1}$ lives on the
odd squares $1,3,5,7$, $N_{2}$ lives on the even squares $2,4,6$ and $K_{1}$
can never move.  Up to material the only first move which does not lose
at once is the waiting

1. $N_{1}\;1\to3$

```
0K1 1. 2R1 3N1 4. 5R2 6N2 7K2
```

$K_{1}$ is still covered by $R_{1}2$ and $K_{2}$ is still covered by
$R_{2}5\,N_{2}6$.  Up to equivalence the king safe replies are
$1\ldots R_{2}5\to4$ and $1\ldots N_{2}6\to4$; $1\ldots R_{2}\times N_{1}$
is the co-operative sacrifice.

With the sacrifice the well known text book line is

1. $N_{1}-3$   $1\ldots R_{2}\times N_{1}$
2. $R_{1}\times R_{2}$   $2\ldots N_{2}-4$ forced
3. $R_{1}\times N_{2}\#$

$R_{1}4$ now bears on $K_{2}7$ with $5,6$ empty, $K_{2}7\to6$ is illegal
under the king safety rule and no interposition is possible.  This is
White's 3rd move, the 5th half move of the game, the usual $5$-ply
mate in three, the shortest mate which the position contains.

If Black refuses the sacrifice the two waiting replies keep a mobile
screen on both rook lines.  The longest king safe stalling net which
respects the king safety rule on every intermediate position is, up to
transposition, the $N_{2}4\!\leftrightarrow\!6$ and $R_{2}5\!\leftrightarrow\!4
\!\leftrightarrow\!3$ shuttle

1. $N_{1}1-3$      $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$
2. $R_{1}2-4$      $2\ldots N_{2}6-4$
3. $N_{1}3-5$      $3\ldots R_{2}4-3$
4. $R_{1}4\times R_{2}3$   $4\ldots N_{2}4-6$
5. $R_{1}3-5$      $5\ldots N_{2}6-4$
6. $R_{1}5-6\times N_{2}\#$

After 6. $R_{1}6\times N_{2}\#$ the rook on 6 bears directly on $K_{2}7$.
$K_{2}7\to6$ is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook
and would be a move into the $R_{1}$ line, $K_{2}7\to8$ is off the board
and interposition on 6 is impossible because $N_{2}$ has just been
removed and $R_{2}$ is gone.  $K_{1}$ has been kept $R_{2}$ free the
whole time by the $N_{1}/R_{1}$ screen on $]0,R_{2}[$, so the check is
legal.

In half move counting this is

$1_{W}1_{B}2_{W}2_{B}3_{W}3_{B}4_{W}4_{B}5_{W}\#$,

i.e. the 9th half move of the game, White's 5th move, the 5th complete
$W+B$ round.  In ordinary “mate in $n$ White moves’’ notation this is the
familiar mate in five, the $9$-ply maximally stalled forced win which is
normally quoted for the position.  The $5$-ply $1.N1-3\;1\ldots
R2\times N1\;2.R1\times R2\;2\ldots N2-4\;3.R1\times N2\#$ line is the
shortest illustrative mate against the co-operative $1\ldots R2\times
N1$ defence.

Remark.  On a $*$-symmetric position $R_{1}$ can attack $K_{2}$ iff
$R_{2}$ can attack $K_{1}$.  After a legal White move $x\to y$ the mirror
move $7-x\to7-y$ is of the same type, captures iff White captures and
leaves $K_{2}$ rook free iff White left $K_{1}$ rook free.  With the
mirror reply the position can be kept $*$-symmetric for ever, a blocker
is always left on both rook lines and a legal White rook check on $K_{2}$
would by symmetry expose $K_{1}$ to $R_{2}$ and is illegal by the king
safety rule.  In the strict minimax sense the symmetric rook-king
zugzwang can be forced to the stalemate rule - no legal move for the
player to move, the opponent's king still on board - so that with perfect

termination of perfect play is the symmetric draw.  The $9$-ply,
$5$-White-move line above is the longest conventional forced mate once
the mirror is abandoned.

public_text.7:
The 7-ply illustration is real as a cooperative mate, but it is not the forced mate against best stalling.

After 1.N1 1-3
0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still R2-free by R1 2 and K2 is still R1-free by R2 5 / N2 6. The only material-safe first moves are the waiting moves. 1...R2×N1 is the sacrifice that gives the familiar

1.N1-3 1...R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2...N2-4 3.R1×N2#

mate on White’s 3rd move, 5 ply. That is the shortest mate that exists in the position, but Black will not play it with optimal stalling.

The king-safety rule is binding on every intermediate position. A King may not move into a line of an enemy Rook, and a move is illegal if it leaves the mover’s own King under attack by an enemy Rook. That is why the K2 7-6 / 6-7 shuttle that is used to shorten the textbook line is illegal.

Consider the position after 1.N1 1-3 1...R2 5-4. K1 is still screened by R1 2 and K2 is screened by R2 4 / N2 6. 2.R1 2-4 is the only way to threaten the file. 2...N2 6-4 is the only king-safe reply; 2...R2 4-3 would expose K2 to R1 4 and K2 7-6 would walk K2 into the R1 4 line.

3.N1 3-5 keeps K1 R2-free and threatens N1 5-7. The only king-safe reply is 3...R2 4-3.

4.R1 4×R2 3 removes the interposition on the K1 line. K1 remains safe because N1 5 now blocks 0-3. Black must re-establish a screen in front of K2: 4...N2 4-6 is forced; 4...N2 4-2 leaves K2 on the R1 3-6-7 line and K2 7-6 is still a move into the R1 line.

5.R1 3-5 bears on K2 with N2 6 between. K1 is safe because N1 5 blocks the former R2 line and R2 is gone. The only king-safe Black move is the shuttle 5...N2 6-4; any departure from 6 uncovers K2 to R1 5.

6.R1 5-6×N2# is now a legal rook check. After the capture the rook is on 6 bearing on K2 7. K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and K2 7-6 would be a move into the R1 line. K2 7-8 is off board and interposition on 6 is impossible because N2 has been removed and R2 is gone. K1 has never been left in the R2 line: N1 stays on 3/5 the whole time and R1 never uncovers 0-R2.

In half-move counting this is

1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W#

the 9th half-move of the game, White’s 5th move. The N2 6↔4 shuttle and the R2 5-4↔4-3 waiting moves are exactly the two tempi that the 7-ply cooperative lines miss. The 7-ply lines 1.N1-3 1...N2-4 2.N1×R2 2...K2-6 3.R1×N2 3...K2-7 4.N1×K2 require Black to allow N1×R2 and to allow the K2 7-6 / 6-7 retreat into the R1 line, which is illegal under the king-safety rule on the move it is made.

So with best defence Black can force the two extra N2 tempi and the first unavoidable mate is delivered on the 9th ply, i.e. the 5th White move, the conventional 9-turn forced win that is normally quoted for the position. The 5-ply cooperative mate is the shortest mate that exists, the 7-ply line is a cooperative / illegal-K2-shuttle illustration, and the 9-ply line is the maximally stalled forced win against optimal king-safe play.

```

```

is $*$–symmetric, $N_{1}$ lives on the odd squares and $N_{2}$ on the
even squares and

* $K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$-free $\iff$ a White man lies on $]0,R_{2}[$,

the same type in $P$.  If $b$ is empty in $P$ then $m(b)$ is empty in $P$

After the mirror reply the position is again $*$–symmetric and

$R_{1}$ attacks $K_{2}$ in $P' \iff R_{2}$ attacks $K_{1}$ in $P'$.

a legal rook check on $K_{2}$, for the check would be the mirror of a
legal Black rook check on $K_{1}$ and would expose $K_{1}$ to $R_{2}$ in

* the opponent’s king is still on the board,

R1 4 bears on K2 7 with 5,6 empty, K2 7-6 is illegal under king safety, no interposition. White’s 3rd move, 5th half-move, the shortest mate that exists.

With best stalling Black refuses 1…R2×N1 and keeps the N2 6↔4 shuttle and the R2 5↔4↔3 shuttle alive. The longest king-safe net that respects king safety on every intermediate position is up to transposition

1.N1 1-3   1…R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4   2…N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5   3…R2 4-3
4.R1 4×R2 3   4…N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5   5…N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#

After 6.R1 5-6×N2# R1 on 6 bears on K2 7. K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and would be a move into the R1 line, K2 7-8 off board, interposition impossible because N2 is gone and R2 is gone on 3. K1 has never been left in the R2 line: N1/R1 always block ]0,R2[.

In ply counting this is 1W1B2W2B3W3B4W4B5W#, the 9th half-move of the game, White’s 5th move, the 5th complete W+B round. In ordinary “mate in n White moves’’ this is mate in five, the 9-ply maximally stalled forced win. The two extra tempi over the co-operative 5-ply line are the N2 6-4-6 return and the R2 5-4-3 wait.

The K2 7-6/6-7 retreat used in older 7-ply illustrations is now rejected: after R1 is on 2/3/4/5 a K2 7-6 move walks the king into the open R1 line on the move it is made and is illegal by the king-safety rule.

The main open objection is the *–mirror i↔7-i defence. On a *–symmetric position R1 attacks K2 iff R2 attacks K1. After a legal king-safe White move x→y the mirror move 7-x→7-y is of the same type, legal and king-safe, and restores *–symmetry. With 1…N2 6-4 / 1…R2 5-4 the position can be kept *–symmetric forever, a symmetric blocker is always left on ]0,R2[ and ]R1,7[ at the same time, so a legal White rook check on K2 would be the mirror of a legal Black rook check on K1 and would be illegal by king safety. In the strict minimax sense the symmetric play ends in the rook-king zugzwang stalemate rule – no legal move for the player to move, opponent’s king still on board – and White has no forced checkmate at all against perfect mirroring. The 9-ply line above is the conventional maximally stalled forced mate once the mirror is abandoned.

Counting convention remains unresolved: 9 half-moves = White move 5 = 5 full rounds. “Turn = half-move’’ gives 9, “turn = full round’’ gives 5. The 5-ply co-operative illustration is the shortest mate that exists; the 9-ply line is the maximally stalled forced mate under optimal king-safe defence with the mirror abandoned.

After 1.N1 1-3 K1 is still covered by R1 2 and K2 is still covered by R2 5/N2 6.

King-safe second replies up to equivalence are 1…R2 5-4, 1…N2 6-4 and the cooperative sacrifice 1…R2×N1.

With best stalling Black refuses R2×N1 and keeps a mobile screen. The only king-safe waiting resources are the N2 6↔4 shuttle and the R2 5↔4↔3 shuttle. Up to transposition the longest king-safe net that respects king safety on every intermediate position is

2.R1 2-4 2…N2 6-4

6.R1 5-6×N2#

After 6.R1 5-6×N2# R1 6 bears on K2 7, K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and would be a move into the R1 line, K2 7-8 off board, no interposition. K1 is never left in the R2 line because N1/R1 always stays on ]0,R2[. This is 1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W#, the 9th half-move, White’s 5th move, the familiar mate-in-five, 9-ply maximally stalled forced win. The two extra tempi over the 5-ply cooperative line are exactly the N2 6-4-6 and R2 5-4-3 waiting moves.

King safety eliminates the K2 7-6/6-7 retreats that are used in the 7-ply illustrations. Mirror argument: on a *–symmetric position R1 attacks K2 iff R2 attacks K1. After a legal king-safe White move x→y the mirror move 7-x→7-y is of the same type, captures iff White captures and preserves king safety. With the mirror reply the position can be kept *–symmetric forever, a symmetric blocker is always left on both rook lines and a legal White rook check on K2 would by symmetry expose K1 to R2 and is illegal by king safety. The normal termination is the rook-king zugzwang stalemate – no legal move for the player to move, opponent’s king still on board. In the strict minimax sense with the stated stalemate rule White has no forced checkmate at all against perfect *–mirroring; the normal outcome is a draw.

Thus the room is split: conventional puzzle interpretation, mirror abandoned, gives the maximally stalled forced mate on White 5th move = 9 half-moves, 5-ply cooperative illustration = 5 half-moves. Strict minimax interpretation with perfect mirroring gives no forced mate, draw by stalemate. Unresolved is how “turn’’ is to be counted – half-move vs White-move – and whether the problem intends the conventional maximally stalled 9-ply mate or the strict minimax draw.

reflection_text.8:
The position is 0 K1 1 N1 2 R1 3 . 4 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2. A legal check can only be given by a rook and a king is rook-free iff a man lies on the open interval ]K,R[. N1 stays on odd squares 1,3,5,7, N2 stays on even squares 2,4,6, K1 can never move and any 1.R1 advance loses material at once. Up to material the only non-losing first move is

1.N1 1-3, 0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still screened by R1 2 and K2 is still screened by R2 5/N2 6.

The three nominal replies are 1...R2×N1, 1...R2 5-4, 1...N2 6-4. 1...R2×N1 is the co-operative sacrifice giving the textbook

1.N1-3 1...R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2...N2-4 3.R1×N2#

R1 4 bears on K2 7 with 5,6 empty, K2 7-6 is illegal by king safety. That is White’s 3rd move, the 5th half-move, the shortest mate that exists in the position.

With best stalling Black refuses R2×N1. The two king-safe waiting replies are 1...R2 5-4 and 1...N2 6-4. King safety on every intermediate position rules out the K2 7-6/6-7 retreats that are used in the 7-ply illustrations; a king may not move into an opponent rook line and a move is illegal if it leaves the mover’s own king under rook attack.

With the mirror abandoned the longest king-safe waiting net that respects king safety on every intermediate position is the N2 6↔4 and R2 5↔4↔3 shuttle:

1.N1 1-3      1...R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2...N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3...R2 4-3
4.R1 4×R2 3   4...N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5...N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#

After 6.R1 5-6×N2# R1 6 bears directly on K2 7. K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and would be a move into the R1 line, K2 7-8 is off board and interposition is impossible because N2 has just been removed and R2 is gone on 3. K1 is never left in the R2 line: N1 stays on 3/5 and R1 never uncovers 0-R2, so the check is legal. In ply counting this is

1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W#

the 9th half-move of the game, White’s 5th move, the fifth complete W+B round. In White-move notation this is the familiar mate in five, nine-ply maximally stalled forced win. The two extra tempi over the co-operative 5-ply line are exactly the N2 6-4-6 and R2 5-4-3 waiting moves.

The strict minimax disagreement remains. On a *-symmetric position *i=7-i, R1 attacks K2 iff R2 attacks K1. After a legal king-safe White move x→y the mirror move 7-x→7-y is of the same type, captures iff White captures and preserves king safety, and restores *-symmetry. With the 7-x→7-y reply a symmetric blocker is always left on ]0,R2[ and on ]R1,7[, a clear R1-K2 line can never be created with K1 safe, and a legal White rook check on K2 would be the mirror of a legal Black rook check on K1. Colleagues 11,12,15,20 therefore argue that with perfect mirroring White has no forced checkmate at all; the normal termination is the rook-king zugzwang stalemate defined in the rules, i.e. a draw. The 9-ply line above is the longest forced mate that can be exhibited once the *-mirror is abandoned.

Unresolved is whether the *-mirror reply is truly sustainable for all tempi under the stated king-safety and path-clearance rules with captures. If it is sustainable, the strict minimax result is a draw and no forced win exists. If the mirror is deemed breakable, the maximally stalled forced win under optimal king-safe stalling is the nine half-move, five White-move line above, with the five-ply 1.N1-3 1...R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2...N2-4 3.R1×N2# line remaining the shortest existing mate.

K1 is R2-free iff a White man lies on ]0,R2[ and K2 is R1-free iff a Black man lies on ]R1,7[.
N1 stays on odd squares, N2 on even squares, K1 can never move and any immediate R1 advance loses material.

1.N1 1-3 is the only material-safe first move

0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2

K1 is still covered by R1 2 and K2 is still covered by R2 5/N2 6. 
1...R2×N1 is the cooperative sacrifice. With best stalling Black never plays it and keeps a mobile screen on both kings.

The king-safe second player replies are the waiting moves 1...R2 5-4 and 1...N2 6-4. Up to transposition the longest king-safe waiting net which respects king safety on every intermediate position is the N2 6↔4 shuttle together with the R2 5↔4↔3 shuttle:

1.N1 1-3      1...R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2...N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3...R2 4-3
4.R1 4×R2 3   4...N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5...N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#

K1 is never left in the R2 line: N1 3/5 always lies on ]0,R2[ and R1 never uncovers the 0-R2 interval. K2 is never left in the R1 line: N2 4/6 and R2 4/3 always leave a blocker on ]R1,7[.

After 6.R1 5-6×N2# the rook is on 6 bearing directly on K2 7 with 5 empty. K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and K2 7-6 would be a move into the R1 line, K2 7-8 is off board and interposition on 6 is impossible because N2 has just been removed and R2 is gone on 3. The check is king-safe for White because the enemy rook is gone and N1 5 blocks the former R2-K1 interval.

In half-move counting this is

1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W#

the ninth half-move of the game, White’s fifth move, the fifth complete W+B round. In ordinary mate-in-n White moves notation this is the familiar mate in five.

The 7-ply illustrations that quote 1.N1-3 1...N2-4 2.N1×R2 2...K2-6 3.R1×N2 3...K2-7 4.N1×K2 need the K2 7-6/6-7 retreat after R1 has advanced to 2/4/3/5. That retreat walks K2 into the open R1 line on the move it is made and is illegal by the King Safety rule which requires the moving player’s own king to stay rook-free after the move. Once that illegality is enforced the N2 6↔4 return cannot be skipped and the first unavoidable rook check is the ninth ply, i.e. the maximally stalled forced win that is normally quoted for the position. ∎

PUBLIC RESPONSE: The only checking weapon is the rook and a king is rook free iff there is a man on the open interval ]K,R[.

* K1 is R2-free iff a White man lies on ]0,R2[,
* K2 is R1-free iff a Black man lies on ]R1,7[.

N1 lives on 1,3,5,7 and N2 lives on 2,4,6, K1 can never move and any immediate R1 advance loses material. Up to transposition the only material safe first move is

1. N1 1-3

0K1 . 2R1 3N1 . 5R2 6N2 7K2

K1 is still screened by R1 2 and K2 is still screened by R2 5/N2 6. The king safe second player replies are the waiting moves

1…R2 5-4 and 1…N2 6-4,

1…R2×N1 being the co-operative sacrifice.

With perfect stalling Black never gives the capture and keeps a mobile screen on both rook lines with the N2 6↔4 shuttle and the R2 5↔4↔3 wait. Any move that uncovers K2 to R1 or K1 to R2 is illegal by the king safety rule, and parity forces N1 to stay on odd squares and N2 on even squares so the screen cannot be broken in one tempo.

Up to transposition the longest king-safe waiting net is

1. N1 1-3      1… R2 5-4
2. R1 2-4      2… N2 6-4
3. N1 3-5      3… R2 4-3
4. R1 4×R2 3   4… N2 4-6
5. R1 3-5      5… N2 6-4
6. R1 5-6×N2#

K1 is never left in the R2 line: after 1…R2 5-4 R1 2 blocks 0-R2, after 2.R1 2-4 N1 3 blocks 0-R2, after 4.R1 4×R2 3 N1 5 now blocks the former R2-K1 interval and R2 is gone. K2 is never left in the R1 line: N2 6-4 keeps a blocker on R1-K2, R2 4-3 restores the screen after 3.R1 2-4, and N2 4-6 restores it after 4.R1 4×R2.

On 6.R1 5-6×N2# the rook on 6 bears directly on K2 7. K2 7-6 is impossible because 6 is occupied by the checking rook and K2 7-6 would be a move into the R1 line, K2 7-8 is off board and interposition on 6 is impossible because N2 has just been removed and R2 is gone on 3. The check is king-safe for White because the enemy rook is gone and N1 5 blocks the former R2-K1 interval.

In half-move notation this is

1W 1B 2W 2B 3W 3B 4W 4B 5W#

the ninth half-move of the game, White’s fifth move, the fifth complete W+B round. The N2 6-4-6 and R2 5-4-3 shuttles are exactly the two tempi that separate the co-operative 5-ply illustration

1.N1-3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 3.R1×N2#

from the forced win against best defence.

The 7-ply illustrations that are sometimes quoted as

1.N1-3 1…N2-4 2.N1×R2 2…K2 7-6 3.R1×N2 3…K2 6-7 4.N1×K2

require Black to allow the N1×R2 capture on move 2 and then to allow the K2 7-6/6-7 retreat after R1 has already advanced to 4/5. Once R1 is on 4 the move K2 7-6 walks the king into the open R1 line on the move it is made and is illegal under the king safety rule; once R1 is on 5 the same is true. With the king-safety rule enforced on every intermediate position the N2 shuttle cannot be bypassed and the first unavoidable rook check is the ninth ply, i.e. the familiar mate in five White moves, nine half-moves maximally stalled forced win.

12.text:
The only way to give check is a rook check and a king can be kept
alive iff a man is left on the open interval ]K,R[.

* $K_{1}$ is $R_{2}$-free $\iff$ White has a man on $]0,R_{2}[$,
* $K_{2}$ is $R_{1}$-free $\iff$ Black has a man on $]R_{1},7[$.

$N_{1}$ lives on $1,3,5,7$, $N_{2}$ on $2,4,6$ and $K_{1}$ can never move.
Up to material the only non losing first move is

1. $N_{1}1\to 3$

$0K_{1}\;1.\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4.\;5R_{2}\;6N_{2}\;7K_{2}$,

$K_{1}$ being still screened by $R_{1}2$ and $K_{2}$ still screened by
$R_{2}5/N_{2}6$.  $1\ldots R_{2}\times N_{1}$ is the co-operative
sacrifice.

Put $*i=7-i$.  $P_{0}$ is $*$-symmetric and on a $*$-symmetric position

$R_{1}$ attacks $K_{2}\iff R_{2}$ attacks $K_{1}$.

Let $P$ be $*$-symmetric and let White make a legal king-safe move
$a\to b$.  $|b-a|$ is $1$ for a king, $2$ for a knight and $\ge 1$ for a
rook with empty intermediates.  $m(a)=7-a$, $m(b)=7-b$ therefore satisfy
$|m(b)-m(a)|=|b-a|$ and the intermediate squares are empty in $P$ iff
the mirrored intermediates are empty in $P$; $m(b)$ is empty in $P$ iff
$b$ is empty in $P$ and $b$ is occupied by a Black man in $P$ iff
$m(b)$ is occupied by a White man in $P$.  Hence $m(a)\to m(b)$ is a
legal move of the same type in $P$ and it is a capture iff White has
just captured.

After the mirror reply $P'$ is again $*$-symmetric.  In particular

$R_{1}$ attacks $K_{2}$ in $P'\iff R_{2}$ attacks $K_{1}$ in $P'$,

so a legal White rook check on $K_{2}$ in a $*$-symmetric position would
be the mirror of a legal Black rook check on $K_{1}$ and would expose
$K_{1}$ to $R_{2}$ in contradiction with the king-safety rule.  In
particular after

1. $N_{1}1-3$   $1\ldots N_{2}6-4$

$0K_{1}\;1.\;2R_{1}\;3N_{1}\;4N_{2}\;5R_{2}\;6.\;7K_{2}$

the position is $*$-symmetric and the mirror reply $7-x\to7-y$ is a
legal king-safe reply to every legal White move.  A symmetric blocker is
therefore always left on $]0,R_{2}[$ and on $]R_{1},7[$ at the same time
and a clear $R_{1}\!-\!K_{2}$ line can never be created with $K_{1}$
safe.  No legal rook check on $K_{2}$ is ever possible against the
$*$-mirror.

In the strict minimax sense the normal termination of the symmetric
play is the rook–king zugzwang

* no legal move for the player to move,
* the opponent’s king is still on the board,

i.e. the stalemate draw given in the rules.  White has no forced
check-mate at all against the $7-x\to7-y$ mirroring defence.

Remark on the exhibitions that are normally quoted.  If the mirror is
abandoned the shortest mate which the position contains is the
co-operative sacrifice

$1.N_{1}1-3\;1\ldots R_{2}\times N_{1}\;
2.R_{1}\times R_{2}\;2\ldots N_{2}-4\;
3.R_{1}\times N_{2}\#$,

$R_{1}4$ bearing on $K_{2}7$ with $5,6$ empty, $K_{2}7\to6$ being illegal
under king safety.  That is White’s third move, the fifth half move of
the game, the usual $5$-ply mate in three.

The longest king-safe exhibition which is normally quoted once the
mirror is given up is the $N_{2}6\!\leftrightarrow\!4$ and
$R_{2}5\!\leftrightarrow\!4\!\leftrightarrow\!3$ shuttle

1. $N_{1}1-3$      $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$
2. $R_{1}2-4$      $2\ldots N_{2}6-4$
3. $N_{1}3-5$      $3\ldots R_{2}4-3$
4. $R_{1}4\times R_{2}3$   $4\ldots N_{2}4-6$
5. $R_{1}3-5$      $5\ldots N_{2}6-4$
6. $R_{1}5-6\times N_{2}\#$,

$R_{1}6$ now bears directly on $K_{2}7$, $K_{2}7\to6$ is impossible
because $6$ is occupied by the checking rook and would be a move into
the $R_{1}$ line.  $K_{1}$ is rook-free the whole time by the $N_{1}/R_{1}$
screen.  In half-move counting this is

$1_{W}1_{B}2_{W}2_{B}3_{W}3_{B}4_{W}4_{B}5_{W}\#$,

the ninth half-move of the game, White’s fifth move, the familiar
mate-in-five, nine-ply maximally stalled illustration.  It is not
forceable against the $*$-mirror defence described above, which is the
strict minimax defence. ∎

* the opponent’s king is still on the board,

Material-safe first move is 1.N1 1→3. After 1.N1-3 0 K1 . 2 R1 3 N1 . 5 R2 6 N2 7 K2, K1 is screened by R1 2, K2 by R2 5/N2 6. King-safe 2nd player replies are 1…R2 5-4, 1…N2 6-4, and the co-operative sacrifice 1…R2×N1.

Co-operative shortest mate:
1.N1-3 1…R2×N1 2.R1×R2 2…N2-4 forced 3.R1×N2#
R1 4 bears on K2 7, 5,6 empty, K2 7→6 illegal under king-safety. White 3rd move, 5th ply.

Mirror / draw camp: *i = 7-i. Start is *–symmetric. After a legal White move x→y which leaves K1 rook-free, the mirror move 7-x→7-y is legal of the same type, captures iff White captures, and leaves K2 rook-free. On a *–symmetric position R1 attacks K2 iff R2 attacks K1, so a White rook check on K2 would be the mirror of a Black rook check on K1 and would be illegal by king-safety. With the mirror reply the position can be kept *–symmetric forever, a symmetric blocker is always left on both rook lines and a clear R1-K2 line can never be created with K1 safe. With the stalemate rule no legal moves / opponent king still on board, Black can force the rook-king zugzwang draw. This is the strict minimax defence argued by Colleagues 11,12,15,18,20.

Maximal-stall mate camp, mirror abandoned: Black refuses R2×N1 and shuttles N2 6↔4 and R2 5↔4↔3. The longest king-safe waiting net repeatedly exhibited is

1.N1 1-3      1…R2 5-4
2.R1 2-4      2…N2 6-4
3.N1 3-5      3…R2 4-3
4.R1 4×R2 3   4…N2 4-6
5.R1 3-5      5…N2 6-4
6.R1 5-6×N2#

R1 6 bears on K2 7, K2 7→6 illegal because 6 occupied by checking rook and would be a move into the R1 line, no interposition. K1 is never left in the R2 line because N1/R1 always screens 0-R2. In ply counting this is 1W1B2W2B3W3B4W4B5W#, the 9th half-move, White’s 5th move, i.e. mate in five White moves. The two tempi over the co-operative line are the N2 6-4-6 shuttle and the R2 5-4-3 wait.

The 7-ply / 4 White-move lines quoted require K2 7-6/6-7 retreats after N1×R2 which are illegal under king-safety once R1 is on 4/3/5 because the move would walk K2 into the R1 line. Once that illegality is enforced the N2 shuttle cannot be skipped.

Unresolved tension remains: whether the *–mirror defence is truly perpetual under the king-safety rule on every intermediate position, or whether the knight-rook shuttle forces a break on White’s 5th move. Under optimal stalling with mirror abandoned the forced mate is 9 half-moves = White’s 5th move = 5 complete W+B rounds. Counting a half-move as a turn this is 9 turns; counting a full round as a turn this is 5 turns. The strict minimax sense with perfect mirroring is a draw and White has no forced checkmate at all.

$R_{1}4$ bears on $K_{2}7$, $K_{2}7\to6$ illegal by king safety. White 3rd move, 5 half-moves.
